bullets.title: FOMC hike near-certain Wednesday; 10-year hits 5% for first time since 2007
bullets.body: CME FedWatch pricing 92.5% probability of a 25bp hike announced Wednesday; market pricing ~76bp additional hikes by 2027 Q1. The 10-year UST yield broke above 5% (highest since 2007) driven by elevated oil prices, Middle East tensions, and supply concerns. JPM lays out five SPX scenarios ranging from -1.75% (no hike) to +1% (hike with prior eases reversed); consensus view is that a 25bp hike as priced would be a clearing event for buy flows.

bullets.title: AI safety debate triggers historic semis/software rotation; trade stabilizing Tuesday
bullets.body: Monday saw Software (IGV) outperform Semis (SOX) by ~12.5% — a 2.4-sigma move, described as 'one of the most epic in-sector divergences of all time' — following Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei's comments calling for slower frontier model development. By Tuesday pre-market semis were rebounding (INTC +2%, NVDA/AVGO +75bps) as investor consensus coalesced around the view that a genuine AI spending slowdown is unlikely, with AI safety manageable through engineering rather than pause. JPM sees the episode as rotating capital from training/chip-dependent plays into inference, hyperscalers, and consumer AI.

bullets.title: NVDA and AVGO management dismiss AI slowdown; AVGO reaffirms $115B FY27 AI revenue target
bullets.body: Both CEOs publicly pushed back against slowdown fears at the Communacopia/All-In conferences. Broadcom CEO Hock Tan explicitly reaffirmed his FY27 AI semiconductor revenue target of $115B; Jensen Huang framed AI as an industrial revolution requiring sustained capex and argued safety is an engineering problem. Citi maintains Buy on both; NVDA PT $315 (~21x C27E), AVGO PT $515 (19x F28). Rubin platform early results show 7x token throughput per megawatt vs. Blackwell (vs. Jensen's prior 3x claim), implying 2x+ more profit per gigawatt.

bullets.title: Oil above $103; geopolitical premium building on Saudi pipeline, Iran, Houthis
bullets.body: WTI rose ~2% above $103.50/bbl on Saudi East-West pipeline shutdown (3-5 weeks for drone-strike repair), Houthi attacks rerouting exports through Hormuz, and Iran's rejection of U.S. negotiations. Goldman Sachs warns Brent could exceed $120/bbl if Gulf production remains significantly below pre-war levels. Rising diesel costs (+120% YOY) are compounding input cost pressures across food, beverage, and logistics sectors.

bullets.title: Semis de-rating on 2028-29 growth moderation fears, not 2027 — buy near-term upgrade candidates
bullets.body: Jefferies and Wolfe both argue the SOX pullback reflects the market pricing a potential 2028-29 moderation, not a change in 2026-27 demand. Management teams at Communacopia were universally bullish: AMAT has 8 quarters of order visibility through 2028; AMD datacenter expected to >2x in CY27; clean-room space constraints make overbuild difficult. Best positioning in stocks with significant near-term EPS estimate upgrade potential and lower multiples; prefer inference and ASIC plays over training-leveraged names.

bullets.title: Rotation playbook: long hyperscalers/inference, short training-leveraged; software over semis
bullets.body: JPM, Hedgeye, and GS all describe similar rotation: long GOOGL, META, MSFT (inference/hyperscaler beneficiaries), short CIEN and later-cycle WFE names. Hedgeye explicitly favors IGV (software) and XLV (healthcare) over semis and industrials; XLI is down 8.3% Q3 YTD. CSCO flagged as a lower-beta inference rotation. Memory names pressured by DeepSeek V4.1 memory innovations and loop-transformer architecture signals from GPT-6 Astra suggesting labs are not aggressively scaling parameters.

bullets.title: US power shortfall of 50-80 GW by 2030 as hyperscaler capex tracks to exceed $1T in 2027
bullets.body: JPM's BTM distributed power deep-dive shows 5-year utility grid load growth forecasts increased 7x (from 24 GW to 166 GW) since 2023, with data centers comprising 55% of incremental demand by 2030. Grid interconnection queues run 5+ years versus BTM capacity deliverable in 12-18 months. Jensen Huang stated power — not chips — is the main AI compute bottleneck. Five major hyperscalers (META, GOOGL, AMZN, MSFT, ORCL) capex on track to exceed $1 trillion in 2027.

bullets.title: Hedgeye macro: bond yields at cycle highs, exit gold/copper; S&P bullish range 7551-7750
bullets.body: UST 2-year and 10-year hit new cycle highs of 4.70% and 5.05% respectively; Hedgeye's 10-year target is 5.05% with inflation not abating near-term. They exited all gold (GDX), copper (ICOP), and silver (SLV) positions on TREND breakdown, and are short duration (TLT, LQD, ZROZ). VIX signal flipped from Neutral to Bullish. S&P 500 risk range 7551-7750 (bullish); Russell 2000 2852-2960 (bearish).

bullets.title: AI regulation risk framed as manageable; narrow rules unlikely to dent profitability, may ease public concerns
bullets.body: Wolfe Research and Jefferies both argue AI doomsday/extinction risk narratives carry regulatory implications but that narrow rules barely dent sector profitability. Bipartisan Klobuchar-Cruz AI safety bill gaining momentum. US projected to control 80% of global compute by 2027 via supply chain dominance and export controls; China expected to close gap post-2030. Cybersecurity and cloud infrastructure flagged as direct beneficiaries of increased safety spending.

bullets.title: SaaS multiples under pressure: All-SaaS index -3.9% YTD at 5.5x FY+2 EV/Sales vs S&P +12.7%
bullets.body: Wolfe's All-SaaS index trades at 5.5x FY+2 EV/Sales, down 2.69% week-over-week and -3.9% YTD, a stark underperformance versus the S&P 500's +12.7% YTD. Pre-market software names (HUBS, TEAM, NOW, RDDT) all down ~2.4%; ADBE and ACN -2%. The Software > Semis pair trade is being widely discussed but near-term SaaS fundamentals remain pressured by elevated rates.

bullets.title: JPM upgrades META to Overweight; names AMZN, GOOGL, SPOT as top Internet picks for 2H
bullets.body: JPM's Fall 2026 Internet sector update upgrades META to Overweight focused on AI models and agents. Top large-cap picks are AMZN, GOOGL, and SPOT; SHOP and TTWO are top SMID picks. Separately, 25 S&P companies quantified AI impact at ~150bp average profit margin improvement; US Cloud sales up 50% y/y with backlogs >100% of sales, though only 8% of enterprises have deployed AI agents at scale.

bullets.title: OpenAI outpacing Anthropic in Q3; enterprise LLM spend stalls for first time in Aug/Sept
bullets.body: Hedgeye's LLM tracker shows OpenAI (Codex) grew 400-500% QoQ users in Q3, outpacing Anthropic's sequential growth which cooled sharply in August/September. Enterprise genAI platform spend on global LLMs did not grow sequentially for the first time in Aug/Sept as LLM token prices fell sharply in a global price war. Anthropic ARR/revenue grew 145%/142% QoQ in June 2026 but is at risk if September shows only ~30% sequential growth.

bullets.title: Musk: Taiwan chip dependence is AI scaling bottleneck; Tesla-SpaceX Austin fab as hedge
bullets.body: On the All-In podcast, Musk flagged Taiwan semiconductor dependence and limited fab capacity as the primary near-term AI scaling risk. Tesla and SpaceX are building an R&D semiconductor fab in Austin to secure chip supply. SpaceX plans to launch AI compute satellites next year and is building out compute rental as a major business with no demand slowdown. Musk left open the possibility of a Tesla-SpaceX combination.

bullets.title: China August retail sales miss at +0.4% YoY; credit growth at record low 4.9% YoY
bullets.body: China's August retail sales came in at +0.4% YoY, well below the +0.8% consensus and down from +0.6% in July, weighed by weather and weak underlying demand. Gold & jewelry declined 18% YoY. Separately, China's August credit data were the weakest in 20+ years, with new loans only 60bn yuan and loan growth falling to a record low 4.9% YoY. JPM sees consensus estimates for 2H sector earnings rebound of +21% as overly optimistic.

bullets.title: Truist: PCE growth to decelerate 150-200bps over 12-18 months; savings rate at near 3%
bullets.body: Truist flags US personal savings rate has fallen to ~3%, below long-term average, and PCE growth outpaced disposable income in Q2 2026. Issuer data show a slowdown in volume growth in August. Expect 150-200bp deceleration in PCE growth over the next 12-18 months, though Truist notes this is largely priced into payment stocks. Wage growth running at 4% y/y with lower-end consumers relatively stronger, benefiting neobanks.

bullets.title: BoJ expected to hike 25bp this week; USD/JPY seen as cheap vs fair value
bullets.body: Morgan Stanley expects BoJ to raise its policy rate by 25bp at its September meeting, with 50bp seen as unlikely. Market pricing for a terminal rate above 2% is viewed as overly aggressive. Recent JPY strength is attributed to short-term carry unwinds and GPIF repatriation speculation rather than fundamentals. MS recommends buying USD/JPY into renewed JPY strength.

bullets.title: SB Energy IPO: NVDA commits $1.5B; SoftBank targets $50B valuation for data center + power platform
bullets.body: SB Energy filed for a US Nasdaq IPO (ticker 'SBE') targeting a $50B valuation. The company operates 8.8 GW-IT of signed data center capacity and 5.5 GWac of contracted power with a ~$439B backlog. NVIDIA has contractually committed to purchase $1.5B in non-voting equity at IPO price and serves as residual value guarantor. Strategic investors also include SoftBank and OpenAI.

bullets.title: Semis sector de-rating: SOX -5.9% Monday; physical capacity constraints prevent overbuild narrative
bullets.body: Wolfe's Communacopia takeaways: management conviction remained high across semiconductor companies despite the Monday selloff, which Wolfe characterizes as multiple compression rather than a fundamental change. Clean room space constraints and AI infrastructure bottlenecks require unprecedented customer visibility (AMAT has 8 quarters of order visibility). Physical constraints make overbuild difficult over the next year or longer. Jefferies sees the de-rating as focused on 2028-29 concerns, not 2027.

bullets.title: GS: Equities can absorb 10Y yields up to 5.6-5.7% given 20%+ forward EPS growth
bullets.body: Goldman Sachs maintains a bullish stance on US equities despite rising rates, noting S&P 500 P/E has already compressed to 19x from 22x YTD. JPM's international briefing echoes this, arguing equities can handle yields up to 5.6-5.7% given 20%+ forward EPS growth at current 18x valuation. US equity ETF flows are at their most negative since late Q1 2026 (-2z on 1wk and 4wk basis); CTA positioning in crude is near the 85th percentile.

bullets.title: BofA CEO: Q3 S&T revenue flat Y/Y, IB down ~10% to $1.6-1.8B; Citi IB up low-single-digits
bullets.body: BofA CEO Moynihan guided Q3 S&T revenue flat year-over-year and investment banking fees down ~10% to $1.6B-$1.8B. Citi CFO Luchetti struck a more constructive tone, guiding IB revenue to grow in the low single digits in Q3. Consumer credit quality remains stable: AXP August net charge-offs were 1.7% (stable M/M) and BFH's delinquency rate improved to 5.36% from 5.84% Y/Y.
